clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old primigravida woman with chronic hypertension and morbid obesity had an initial urinary tract infection at 6 weeks gestation with microscopic hematuria. At 27 weeks gestation, she developed dysuria, persistent microscopic hematuria, and a urine culture showed mixed bacterial flora. Two weeks postpartum, a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis identified a 2x4x2 cm anterior vaginal wall mass consistent with a urethral diverticulum, confirming the diagnosis. Postoperative management included intravenous antibiotics; however, details on surgical procedure and physical examination findings prior to imaging were not reported.
